first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because Mykonos is where the bigger numbers might actually work. The first screen is calm: three decisions, in order, no 'affordable', no prices, no exclamation marks. Her summary for me: one hotel speaks of up to 800 guests, the right exclusive-use question is in there, and there is a VIP lounge at the airport. The rest is paperwork for the family office and travel housekeeping for guests. I read the venue section and the house rules myself.

journey.quote: A Mykonos wedding comes down to three decisions, made in order: whether the ceremony is legal or symbolic, which starts the paperwork clock; the season, read from official climate figures and current travel advice; and the area and kind of venue that suit your guest list.
journey.reaction: Composed and ordered. My assistant can put this in one line for me, which is exactly how I want to receive things.

journey.quote: Its name has long been shorthand for cosmopolitan, luxury holidays.
journey.reaction: Said once, plainly, without gushing. Fine.

journey.section: Resorts with chapels, beach settings and private villas
journey.quote: **Large resorts with several spaces.** For a long guest list, a resort with more than one terrace lets the welcome drinks, the ceremony and the dinner each have their own setting.
journey.reaction: This is the paragraph for us, but it stops at 'several spaces'. The 800-guest line only appears further down, in the venue list. It should be here, where someone with a long list is looking.

journey.section: Resorts with chapels, beach settings and private villas
journey.quote: **Private villas.** A villa gives the wedding party one address and a ceremony no one else walks through.
journey.reaction: Understands privacy. The family in one villa, nobody walking through. I would use that for the days around the wedding.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: The hotel describes its weddings as running from intimate gatherings to large weddings with up to 800 guests, from welcome cocktails to five-course gala dinners.
journey.reaction: Finally a number at our scale. My assistant marked Saint John straight away.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: Ceremonies take place on The Ocean Balcony, just above Psarou beach, for up to 60 guests, and the wedding party can then move to the L'Archipel restaurant and pool area for up to 120.
journey.reaction: Lovely, but 120 is a third of our list. It is the first venue named, so for a moment the page feels written for someone else.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: The hotel offers three named wedding packages, and its own wedding coordinators help with items including municipal paperwork and the marriage licence.
journey.reaction: Three named packages. We would not be choosing from a menu.

journey.quote: Once you have an area and a style in mind, [talk to Wonderland Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding&utm_content=primary).
journey.reaction: Here it is 'Wonderland Concierge'; at the end it is 'Wedded Concierge'. Which is it? A small thing, but a house that cannot keep its own name straight makes my assistant pause.

journey.section: When to get married in Mykonos
journey.quote: Plan water, hats, light fabrics, shade and air-conditioned rest for guests, and set a summer ceremony later in the day.
journey.reaction: Right for my grandmother and the older relatives. This is the thinking I want from whoever is on the ground.

journey.quote: Most drownings happen on beaches without a lifeguard or outside lifeguard hours, so point guests to patrolled beaches.
journey.reaction: Earthquakes, drownings, wildfire. Each true, I am sure, but it reads like a government leaflet. My assistant skipped it.

journey.quote: Many couples sign the legal paperwork quietly in Australia, then hold the full ceremony on Mykonos with nothing left to file.
journey.reaction: Quietly. Yes. The legal part done privately at home, the island kept for the family.

journey.quote: A symbolic ceremony also leaves room for customs that matter to your families; read our notes on [Greek wedding traditions](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions) before you talk to a celebrant or venue.
journey.reaction: 'Customs that matter to your families' is said without assuming what ours are. Good. Though the link only points to Greek traditions, not ours.

journey.quote: Requests go on the Document Legalisation Request Form, signed in front of an authorised witness, and can be lodged by appointment at an Australian Passport Office, at many Australian embassies and consulates overseas, or by registered mail to the Authentications Section in Melbourne or Sydney; a fee applies.
journey.reaction: For the family office, not for me. Long, but whoever handles the documents will want it.

journey.quote: It also has accessible travel information for passengers with reduced mobility, worth sending to any guest who needs help on arrival, and a Private Flights Lounge with VIP welcoming services.
journey.reaction: Private flights lounge. That is how half our guests would arrive. Good that it is there, but it is tucked at the end of a sentence after the public bus.

journey.quote: [Mykonos Airport](https://www.jmk-airport.gr/en) lists a direct public bus service and taxis to and from the airport.
journey.reaction: Public bus, first. It pitches the reader as an ordinary traveller.

journey.quote: Some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities, and in most cases passengers carry their own luggage up and down stairs.
journey.reaction: Our guests will not be carrying luggage on a ferry. Advice for a different wedding.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: **Exclusive use.** Will the space, the venue or the whole property be closed to other guests, for how many days, and what does exclusive use cover?
journey.reaction: Exactly my question, including the days. Whoever wrote this has been asked it before.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Correct and discreet. Nothing about our family should sit in a chat thread.

journey.quote: **Exclusive use and the number of days.** Closing a space, a venue or a whole property to other guests, and for how long, shapes the overall cost as much as the guest count does.
journey.reaction: No prices, no 'value'. It talks about what is possible, which is what I want.

journey.quote: **Packages versus extras.** Some venues set out named wedding packages, while others add charges for planner-arranged services such as flowers, DJs, photography and fireworks.
journey.reaction: 'Compare inclusions line by line' is how a package client shops. We would take the property and build from there.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: One person is right, and the close is quiet. 'Quotes in AUD' reminds me again that this was written for an Australian couple, not a family across Dubai, Sydney and London.

unanswered_questions: Can Saint John be closed to the public for three days, and can 300 sit for dinner in one space there?
Could Royal Myconian or the wider Myconian Collection be taken over across more than one property for a large family?
Can our own caterer or chefs work in a hotel kitchen for family dietary and cultural requirements?
Which villas on the island are permitted to host a wedding of our size, or only the family events around it?

turn_offs_found.quote: **Packages versus extras.** Some venues set out named wedding packages, while others add charges for planner-arranged services such as flowers, DJs, photography and fireworks.
turn_offs_found.why: The cost section ends on comparing packages and extras line by line. For a family taking a whole property, packages are not how decisions are made, so it positions me as a standard package client.

turn_offs_found.quote: Some services lack suitable access for people with disabilities, and in most cases passengers carry their own luggage up and down stairs.
turn_offs_found.why: Ferry luggage, public buses, lifeguards and earthquakes add length without anything my family would act on. It reads like a travel leaflet and lowers the sense of a premium service.

turn_offs_found.quote: Most drownings happen on beaches without a lifeguard or outside lifeguard hours, so point guests to patrolled beaches.
turn_offs_found.why: This is safety housekeeping for self-managed guests. My team would brief our guests; I do not need it in a planning guide.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Saint John about a three-day closure and a seated dinner for 300
My mother, for the late-day ceremony advice for older guests and the private villa line

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Mykonos wedding with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=mykonos-wedding&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet, no 'from' price, no pressure, and one person start to finish is right. Mykonos at least shows one venue at our scale. But I would not fill in a web form myself; my assistant might, more likely through a referral.

top_3_changes: In 'Large resorts with several spaces', bring the Saint John line forward (the hotel describes weddings of up to 800 guests across several sea-view spaces) so a reader with a long guest list sees a way forward where she is looking, not only further down the venue list.

Trim the self-managed traveller detail (public bus listed first, ferry luggage, lifeguards, earthquakes) or recast it as a short guest-briefing note, and lead the airport paragraph with the Private Flights Lounge and VIP welcoming services.
Use one name for the concierge service: the primary CTA says 'talk to Wonderland Concierge' while the closing says 'Wedded Concierge'; align the primary CTA link text with the brand term.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why

Title, deferred business details (fees, commissions, private logistics, security, scale proof, on-the-ground team, call first) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request to explain sourcing or not-published items

assumptions: Layla is weighing Mykonos for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
